brief.topic: The Different Lives Inside Two Circles

s01: Two round objects begin on the same slope.
Their insides can change how quickly they roll.
The other is a thin hoop, with its mass near the rim.
We compare equal masses and radii, rolling without slipping.
Falling gives each object energy for both travel and spin.
Mass far from the axis makes rotation harder to change.
The hoop stores more rotational energy at the same forward speed.
From the same height, the cylinder therefore reaches a greater speed.
Here its acceleration is two thirds of gravity along the slope.
The difference comes from mass distribution, not a stronger pull of gravity.
Try releasing them again from farther up.
Both gain more speed, but the cylinder still arrives first.
Enough static friction is needed to keep both from slipping.
Inside a familiar circle, there can be a different way of moving.

scenes.narration:
Two round objects begin on the same slope. Their insides can change how quickly they roll.

One is a solid cylinder. The other is a thin hoop, with its mass near the rim. We compare equal masses and radii, rolling without slipping.

Falling gives each object energy for both travel and spin. Mass far from the axis makes rotation harder to change. The hoop stores more rotational energy at the same forward speed.

From the same height, the cylinder therefore reaches a greater speed. Here its acceleration is two thirds of gravity along the slope. The hoop gets one half. The difference comes from mass distribution, not a stronger pull of gravity.

Try releasing them again from farther up. Both gain more speed, but the cylinder still arrives first. Enough static friction is needed to keep both from slipping. Inside a familiar circle, there can be a different way of moving.
